hypotheses.justification: `DifferentiableOn` is defined in TVS generality (FDeriv/Defs.lean, section TVS: only `[AddCommGroup F] [Module 𝕜 F] [TopologicalSpace F]`). The topology on `ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 M H` comes from Topology/Algebra/Module/Multilinear/Topology.lean (`instTopologicalSpace`, uniform convergence on bounded sets), which needs no finiteness of ι. The normed instances in Multilinear/Basic.lean need `[Fintype ι]`, which `[Finite ι]` does not supply, so even the current statement uses the general topology. Deleting `[Finite ι]` therefore leaves the statement elaborating identically. It stays true for arbitrary ι. `ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply 𝕜 M H u : ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 M H →L[𝕜] H` exists in that same file without finiteness (it needs only `[ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 H]`). Given x ∈ s, take c' with `HasFDerivWithinAt c c' s x`. Its field `isLittleOTVS` says (fun p ↦ c p.1 - c p.2 - c' (p.1 - p.2)) =o[𝕜; L] (fun p ↦ p.1 - p.2). Composing with the evaluation map via `ContinuousLinearMap.isBigOTVS_comp` (Asymptotics/TVS.lean, which assumes only a topology on each space) and `IsBigOTVS.trans_isLittleOTVS` gives the same little-o bound for p ↦ c p.1 u - c p.2 u - ((apply 𝕜 M H u) ∘L c') (p.1 - p.2), equal pointwise by linearity of evaluation. Then `HasFDerivAtFilter.of_isLittleOTVS` gives `HasFDerivWithinAt (fun y ↦ c y u) ((apply 𝕜 M H u) ∘L c') s x`, hence differentiability within s at every x ∈ s. The current proof uses finiteness only because it goes through the Fintype lemma and the chain rule in Comp.lean, which needs the middle space to be normed. The direct TVS argument above does not.
